newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest hog prices steady-off $0.50 - trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest hog prices steady-off $0.50 - trade.

text.p: U.S. Midwest cash hog prices early Monday were steady to $0.50 lower, but could turn higher as the day progresses, dealers said.
Iowa and southern Minnesota hogs were trading $55.00 to $55.50 per cwt in the country and $56.00 to $56.50 at plants.
Illinois hog prices were steady at $55.50 to $57.50 at country buying stations and up to $58.50 for hogs delivered to the plant.
Country buying stations in Indiana were paying $53.50 to $54.00 for hogs and plants were paying $55.00. Ohio hog prices were $54.00 to $55.00 in the country and $56.00 at plants.
Prices were pressured early by light packer demand, but light hog movement could turn prices higher as meat packers compete for live inventory, the livestock dealers said.
Light support also was expected to stem from higher pork prices following last week's holiday-shortened production, the dealers said.
